Now let me check the popover component more carefully. The `popup` style in `popover/styles.css.ts` has `zIndex: 50`, but it's applied to the `Popup` element itself, not to the `Positioner`. In base-ui, the `Positioner` is the element that handles floating positioning, and it needs the z-index to properly layer above other content.

Let me compare:

- **Popover**: `zIndex: 50` on `popup` style (applied to `Popup` element), but **no z-index on `Positioner`**
- **DropdownMenu**: `zIndex: 50` on `positioner` style AND `style={{ zIndex: 50 }}` inline on `Positioner`

- **Tooltip**: `zIndex: 50` on `positioner` style (applied to `Positioner`)
- **Combobox**: `style={{ zIndex: 50 }}` inline on `Positioner`

The problem is clear now — Popover has the z-index on the wrong element. Since the `Positioner` is what creates the stacking context and handles the floating positioning, the z-index needs to be there, not on the child `Popup` element.

Looking at the actual implementation, `PopoverPositioner` just wraps the base-ui `Positioner` without applying any z-index styling, and then `PopoverPanel` places the `PopoverPopup` inside it. This means the z-index is only on the inner element, which could cause stacking problems if the Positioner itself doesn't establish the proper context.

Let me check what the shared menu base styles are doing to see how they handle this differently.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I have a clear picture. Let me summarize the z-index situation across all floating layer components:

| Component        | z-index on Positioner                                                            | z-index on Popup                 |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| **Popover**      | ❌ No                                                                            | ✅ `zIndex: 50` in `popup` style |
| **DropdownMenu** | ✅ `zIndex: 50` in `positioner` style + inline `style={{ zIndex: 50 }}` (double) | ✅ `zIndex: 50` in `popupBase`   |

| **Tooltip** | ✅ `zIndex: 50` in `positioner` style | ❌ No (popup has no z-index) |
| **Combobox** | ✅ `style={{ zIndex: 50 }}` inline | ✅ `zIndex: 50` in `popupBase` |

### Menu Anatomy and Structure

Source: https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/v1.2.0/docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/menu/page.mdx

Demonstrates the basic import and assembly of the Menu component's various parts. It shows how to structure a menu with triggers, portals, positioners, popups, and different item types like Menu.Item, Menu.LinkItem, Menu.Separator, Menu.Group, Menu.RadioGroup, Menu.CheckboxItem, and nested submenus.

```jsx
import { Menu } from '@base-ui/react/menu';

<Menu.Root>
  <Menu.Trigger />
  <Menu.Portal>
    <Menu.Backdrop />
    <Menu.Positioner>
      <Menu.Popup>
        <Menu.Arrow />
        <Menu.Item />
        <Menu.LinkItem />
        <Menu.Separator />
        <Menu.Group>
          <Menu.GroupLabel />
        </Menu.Group>
        <Menu.RadioGroup>
          <Menu.RadioItem />
        </Menu.RadioGroup>
        <Menu.CheckboxItem />
        <Menu.SubmenuRoot>
          <Menu.SubmenuTrigger />
        </Menu.SubmenuRoot>
      </Menu.Popup>
    </Menu.Positioner>
  </Menu.Portal>
</Menu.Root>
````

### Animating Tooltip Position and Size (CSS)

Source: https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/v1.2.0/docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/tooltip/page.mdx

Provides guidance on animating the tooltip's position and size using CSS transitions. Position animations are achieved by transitioning `left`, `right`, `top`, and `bottom` on the `Positioner` part, while size animations target `width` and `height` on the `Popup` part.

```css
/* For Positioner */
.your-positioner-class {
  transition:
    left 0.2s ease,
    right 0.2s ease,
    top 0.2s ease,
    bottom 0.2s ease;
}

/* For Popup */
.your-popup-class {
  transition:
    width 0.2s ease,
    height 0.2s ease;
}
```

### Animate Popover with Motion when keepMounted is true

Source: https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/v1.2.0/docs/src/app/(docs)/react/handbook/animation/page.mdx

This snippet demonstrates how to animate a Popover component using Motion when `keepMounted` is true. It utilizes the `render` prop to compose the `<Popup>` with `motion.div` and animates properties based on the `open` state, avoiding `<AnimatePresence>` for components that stay in the DOM.

```jsx
function App() {
  return (
    <Popover.Root>
      <Popover.Trigger>Trigger</Popover.Trigger>
      <Popover.Portal keepMounted>
        <Popover.Positioner>
          <Popover.Popup
            render={(props, state) => (
              <motion.div
                {...(props as HTMLMotionProps<'div'>)}
                initial={false}
                animate={{
                  opacity: state.open ? 1 : 0,
                  scale: state.open ? 1 : 0.8,
                }}
              />
            )}
          >
            Popup
          </Popover.Popup>
        </Popover.Positioner>
      </Popover.Portal>
    </Popover.Root>
  );
}
```

### Base UI Popover API > Position and Size

Source: https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/v1.2.0/docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/popover/page.mdx

To animate the popover's position, apply CSS transitions to the `left`, `right`, `top`, and `bottom` properties of the **Positioner** part. To animate its size, transition the `width` and `height` of the **Popup** part.

Base UI uses portals for components that render popups, such as Dialog and Popover. To make portaled components always appear on top of the entire page, add the following style to your application layout root: This style creates a separate stacking context for your application's `.root` element. This way, popups always appear above the page contents, and any `z-index` property in your styles won't interfere with them.

### Base UI Portal Setup with CSS

Configures the application layout root for Base UI portals. The `isolation: isolate;` style ensures that portaled components, like Dialogs and Popovers, always render on top of the page content by creating a separate stacking context.

.root {
  isolation: isolate;
}
